LRS.title: Reading the whole statute and related provisions
LRS.shortTitle: Reading the whole statute and related provisions
LRS.summary: Structural interpretation reads a disputed phrase alongside the other provisions that define the statutory scheme.
LRS.notes:
Compare definitions, exceptions, related grants of authority, and the consequences of proposed readings across the scheme. In Raila and Dolan, differently worded Federal Tort Claims Act exceptions helped establish the chosen postal exception’s relative scope. In Gayle and Small, the explicit federal-or-state business-offense exception created an anomaly if the general any-court prohibition included foreign convictions.

An anomaly is evidence to evaluate, not a license to repair every asymmetry. Congress may choose uneven rules or a compromise with limited reach. The interpreter must explain why the structural difference supports the proposed meaning and consider a plausible competing explanation, as the Small dissent does.
